title: 10 UI/UX Rules for Developer Portfolios in 2024/2025
transcript:
In this masterclass we break down the definitive UI/UX rules that separate an amateur portfolio from a professional one.
Rule 1: The 3-Second Value Proposition. When someone lands above the fold, they must understand three things within 3 seconds: your name, your exact specialization (e.g. 'Senior Frontend Engineer | React & WebGL'), and proof of work. Do not write 'I create digital dreams' or 'Passionate coder'. Be explicit.
Rule 2: Visual hierarchy and whitespace. The number one mistake developers make is cramming elements together. Give your sections 80px to 120px of vertical padding. Let elements breathe.
Rule 3: Contrast and accessibility. Ensure your text has at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against the background. If using dark mode (#0a0a0a), do not use pure #ffffff for body text—use #e0e0e0 or #cccccc to reduce eye strain, while keeping headings crisp.
Rule 4: Limit your color palette. Pick one primary neutral, one surface color, and one vibrant accent color (e.g. electric cyan, lime, or amber). Never use 6 different accent colors across your buttons.
Rule 5: Bento grids. Use modular bento cards to organize skills, projects, and testimonials. Bento grids create rhythm and clean responsive collapsing on mobile.
